How do I make Explorer my default browser?
Open the settings of your device, go to Apps, then Default apps, then Browser app, and choose Explorer.
The three-dot menu has a Downloads entry that lists what this browser downloaded. The files are in the Downloads folder of your device.

A private tab does not write to the history and is not restored when the browser starts again. Whether it also keeps its cookies apart from normal tabs depends on the WebView of your device; a message says which applies when you open one.

Open Site settings, then Ads. While the switch there is off, ads and trackers are blocked with the filter list you choose on the same screen. With \"Add site exception\" you can allow them for a single site.
Why do websites think I use Google Chrome?

Many websites work badly, or not at all, with browsers they do not know. Explorer therefore introduces itself as Chrome on Android, with the Android version of your device. The Desktop site switch in the three-dot menu makes it introduce itself as Chrome on a computer instead.
I hid the bars. How do I get them back?
Tap the small round button in the top corner of the page.
How do I move my bookmarks to another device?
Use Backup in the settings to save your data to a file, copy the file to the other device, and restore it there with Backup.

xGuard works in two layers. The filter list (the ad blocker, which every site setting for ads follows) takes the hosts on the list out of a page. The tracker blocker knows what kind of tracker a host is and stops the kinds that are switched on. The tracking analysis counts every request a page makes, so it can be seen what was stopped and what was let through. A site whose protection is switched off in the panel behind the shield keeps both layers off.

This extension has nothing to show. Its content scripts work on the pages it asks for.

Explorer unpacks the extension from the Chrome Web Store and runs it itself, because the Android System WebView knows no chrome.* interfaces. Before it is added you are shown what it asks for, as Chrome shows it. Its content scripts and stylesheets run on the pages they ask for, a tap on it opens its own popup or options page in a bubble, its background page runs on its own, and its parts talk through chrome.runtime and chrome.tabs; chrome.storage is kept by Explorer. What is left out is declarativeNetRequest blocking, a background that has to outlive the browser, and the tabs of other windows. Extensions are taken from Google’s servers unchanged; Explorer does not check their signature, so add only extensions you trust.
